extracted.intended_audience: potential grantees, nonprofit organizations, researchers, technologists, and partners interested in funding or collaborating with the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation
extracted.subtask_description: Programmatic priorities and evaluative principles used by the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation to guide investments in AI and data-science-based work aimed at social impact. Covers thematic focus areas, cross-sector collaboration, equity and stewardship principles, capacity-building, and examples of preferred project outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AI and data science for social good / transformative potential
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation "catalyzes the transformative potential of technology to solve humanity’s greatest challenges" by applying AI and data science to produce social benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority to work that demonstrates how AI and data approaches can be harnessed to build more equitable and reliable systems, increase participation and human connection, and democratize resources. Emphasis on projects that translate technological capability into tangible social outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic focus areas (domain relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program investments span digital health, climate change, information technology, neuroscience, educating future generations of technologists, and empowering vulnerable communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should align with one or more of these substantive domains. Examples of funded work include Data Lab/Resource Watch (climate & environment), medical education and evidence programs (health), and programs empowering vulnerable communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply IDEA — inclusion, diversity, equity, and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation applies the principles of IDEA (inclusion, diversity, equity, and accessibility) in the use of AI and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for projects that increase diversity and inclusion in AI education, research, development, and policy (example partnership: AI4All). Proposals should show how they operationalize IDEA in participant recruitment, team composition, design, access, and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen nonprofit capacity to use tech, AI, and data
rubrics_metrics.description: Committed to helping nonprofits unlock capacity to apply data and AI for greater impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports capacity-building activities, partnerships with world-class organizations, and plans to invest in in-house teams or shared resources (the Foundation plans an in-house AI/data team to serve other social change organizations). Proposals that demonstrate sustainable capability-building and knowledge transfer are favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-sector collaboration and ecosystem-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should bring together academia, practitioners, and civil society to pursue AI and data science for shared and greater good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that create convenings, collaborative research-practice partnerships, or multi-stakeholder pilots (examples: Aspen Institute, NationSwell partnerships) are encouraged. Emphasis on building a robust and inclusive ecosystem rather than isolated technical proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-driven data science that guides policy and services
rubrics_metrics.description: Data science should be used to discover knowledge, insight, and evidence that guides policy, scientific inquiry, and service delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for projects that produce actionable evidence, inform decision-making, or create tools/data products (example: Resource Watch) that increase transparency and inform sustainable decisions across climate, energy, food, water, cities, oceans, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerate applications of AI to maximize human potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek new ways to develop and apply AI to produce better social, economic, environmental, and health outcomes and to augment human achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favors translational, applied work that moves AI from research into real-world impact. Example: Rapid Reviews COVID-19 — an AI-powered academic journal accelerating curation and review to help scientists and public health actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate for digital dignity, data stewardship, and ethical technology
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation works to protect data rights and ensure the benefits of data and technology are shared by all, advocating for digital dignity and well-governed access to data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports initiatives that increase access to data in trustworthy ways and that build governance structures (examples: collaboration with the Open Data Institute, pilots for data trusts or data cooperatives). Projects should address governance, stewardship responsibilities, and equitable access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovate technology solutions for pressing global challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance digital and data-driven solutions addressing urgent problems such as health care delivery, hunger, poverty, and climate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for practical technology interventions with measurable impact (examples: Medicapt app to prevent sexual violence; Better Evidence program training medical students). Funded projects should demonstrate relevance to pressing challenges and potential for scale or replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve information quality and reduce misinformation using AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Support uses of AI that accelerate curation of research and reduce misinformation while elevating noteworthy and useful findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects like Rapid Reviews COVID-19 (using custom AI tools to accelerate curation and rapid review) illustrate the kind of information-quality work supported. Proposals should explain how AI reduces misinformation risk and improves the signal-to-noise ratio for target audiences (scientists, public health officials, journalists, public).

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratize resources, increase participation and human connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should aim to democratize access to resources and technology, increase participation, and foster human connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects are favored when they explicitly articulate how they will lower barriers to access, engage diverse communities, and strengthen human-centered outcomes rather than only technical metrics.
